channel.title: The Western Producer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Western Producer (producer.com)

item.title: Canadian trade tribunal to examine imports of frozen, canned vegetables
item.description: Canadian officials will look into whether global imports of frozen and canned vegetables are threatening Canadian growers and processors.

item.title: Gulf fertilizer plants go dark as Iran war chokes global supply ahead of spring planting
item.description: Strait of Hormuz closure halts Gulf fertilizer production, sending urea prices surging as global spring planting season begins.

item.title: BASF announces $27 million Saskatoon breeding facility expansion
item.description: BASF is investing $27 million to expand its Canola Breeding Centre of Innovation in Saskatoon with the hopes of refining and accelerating the development of hybrid canola.

item.title: Cutbacks linked to drop in variety applications
item.description: The Plant Breeders’ Rights Office is receiving fewer applications for IP protection, for wheat and other cereal crop varieties

item.title: Canada’s Farm Show underway in Regina
item.description: Saskatchewan premier Scott Moe opened Canada’s Farm Show in Regina this morning, saying the province has welcomed 61 projects worth $62 billion in the last year.

item.title: Canadian Agricultural Safety Association promotes new vision for farm safety
item.description: The Canadian Agriculture Safety Association announced a new vision and mission statement of promoting a “culture of agricultural safety that protects people through knowledge sharing, support, and meaningful connections” during Canadian Agricultural Safety Week, March 15-21.

item.title: United Farmers of Alberta’s $48.2 million bid for AgraCity awaits court approval
item.description: UFA is the successful bidder for the AgraCity assets subject to approval from the Court of King’s Bench.

item.title: Louis Dreyfus plant provides new delivery option for peas
item.description: SASKATOON — Canadian pea growers have a major new market for their crop. Louis Dreyfus Canada (LDC) began commissioning its pea protein isolate production facility in Yorkton, Sask., earlier this month. “Global demand for pea proteins continues to grow, for its non-allergen and non-GMO status, as well as its versatility across many food applications,” said […] Read more

item.title: Richardson back in the fold at canola council
item.description: Richardson International has rejoined the Canola Council of Canada after a nearly nine-year hiatus.

item.title: Saskatchewan firm wants its camera system to go global
item.description: A Saskatchewan tech startup is one of the 15 agtech companies from across Canada and the United Kingdom to join Cohort 5 of Cultivator powered by Conexus’s AgTech Accelerator.
